proposals.after: Whenever word of a call reached him, he bolted for the deep hills; contemporaries ranked him with Liang Hong and Guan Ning.

proposals.after: He spoke only to Yin Yong and Qi Hao.

proposals.after: Lu Lian never held his tongue—how can I stay silent while men go barbarian?'
proposals.reason: 魯連 is Lu Lian (Lu Zhonglian)

proposals.before: Have you no desire for office?"
proposals.after: Is there nothing you seek?"

proposals.before: Will you not seek a post after all?"
proposals.after: Is there nothing you seek after all?"
proposals.reason: The added government post is unsupported by 子無求乎.

proposals.before: Again the filial daughter Cao E, age just fourteen, her chaste and compliant virtue surpassed Yue, Liang, and Song; her father fell into the river and his body could not be recovered; E looked up to heaven and wailed, midstream sighed in grief, then threw herself into the water and died; father and son lost their corpses; afterward both came out; the people of the state pitied her filial righteousness and for her composed the piece "River Maid.
proposals.after: Again the filial daughter Cao E, age just fourteen, her chaste and compliant virtue surpassed Yue, Liang, and Song; her father fell into the river and his body could not be recovered; E looked up to heaven and wailed, midstream sighed in grief, then threw herself into the water and died; father and daughter lost their corpses; afterward both came out; the people of the state pitied her filial righteousness and for her composed the piece "River Maid.
proposals.reason: 曹娥 is the father's daughter, not his son.

proposals.before: In Xianning 4 the court named him a doctorate; he pleaded illness and stayed away.
proposals.after: In Xianning 4 the court named him an Erudite; he pleaded illness and stayed away.
proposals.reason: 博士 is the court office Erudite, not an academic degree.

proposals.before: Moreover for a plain-robed man to become governor there is precedent in Former Han; it is fitting to hear the brilliance to reward custom and air."
proposals.after: Moreover, Former Han provides precedent for appointing a commoner as governor; his conspicuous advancement should be permitted to encourage prevailing values."
proposals.reason: 宜聽光顯 means permitting conspicuous advancement, not 'hear the brilliance'; 風尚 means prevailing values.

proposals.before: A tiger left a deer at his door; he told neighbors, they sold it and offered him coin.
proposals.after: A wild beast left a deer at his door; he told neighbors, they sold it and offered him coin.
proposals.reason: 猛獸 is an unspecified fierce or wild beast; the source does not identify a tiger.

proposals.before: I mentioned it only because I do not need the silver.'
proposals.after: I mentioned it only because I do not need the money.'

proposals.before: Wen lifted three fingers—he died on the fifteenth day as he signaled.
proposals.after: Wen raised his hand three times—he died on the fifteenth day as he signaled.
proposals.reason: 三舉手 is three raisings of the hand, not three fingers.

proposals.before: Gong Zhuang, styled Ziwei, was a man of Brazil.
proposals.after: Gong Zhuang, styled Ziwei, was a man of Baxi.
proposals.reason: 巴西 is the historical commandery Baxi, not Brazil; this complements the already-proposed idiomatic repair without duplicating it.

proposals.before: His father was killed by Li Te; Zhuang for years did not remove mourning, his strength being weak and unable to avenge.
proposals.after: His father and uncle were killed by Li Te; Zhuang for years did not remove mourning, his strength being weak and unable to avenge.
proposals.reason: 父叔 names both his father and his uncle as victims.

proposals.before: Li Te had his father killed; Zhuang wore mourning for years, too weak to strike back.
proposals.after: Li Te had his father and uncle killed; Zhuang wore mourning for years, too weak to strike back.
proposals.reason: The source expressly includes Gong Zhuang's uncle as well as his father.

proposals.before: Bing Yu was Bing Yuan's heir: silent, careful, every gesture correct.
proposals.after: Bing Yu was Bing Yuan's great-grandson: silent, careful, every gesture correct.
proposals.reason: 曾孫 specifies a great-grandson, not merely an heir.

proposals.before: Qiao Xiu, styled Yuanyan, was a man of Brazil.
proposals.after: Qiao Xiu, styled Yuanyan, was a man of Baxi.
proposals.reason: 巴西 is Baxi commandery; this complements the already-proposed idiomatic repair.

proposals.before: When Li Xiong held Shu and annexed Brazil, Xiong's uncle Xiang and Xiang's son Shou both admired Xiu's name, fully preparing bundled silks and peace carriage to summon him; he answered neither.
proposals.after: When Li Xiong held Shu and occupied Baxi, Xiong's uncle Xiang and Xiang's son Shou both admired Xiu's name, fully preparing bundled silks and a sedan carriage to summon him; he answered neither.
proposals.reason: 巴西 is Baxi, not Brazil; 略有 here means occupying/possessing it, and 安車 is a seated or sedan carriage.

proposals.before: When Fan Ben rose, a hundred clansmen sheltered under his staff.
proposals.after: Soon Fan Ben and Xiao Jing rebelled in succession; Xiu fled to Dangqu, where hundreds of clansmen relied on him.
proposals.reason: The current field omits Xiao Jing, Dangqu, and Qiao Xiu's flight, and reverses who relied on whom.

proposals.before: Emperor Kang again with attendant censor regular summoned Tang; he firmly declined old age and illness and did not arrive.
proposals.after: Emperor Kang again summoned Tang as Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance; he firmly declined on grounds of age and illness and did not arrive.
proposals.reason: 散騎常侍 is Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance, not an attendant censor.

proposals.before: Emperor Kang summoned him as attendant censor; again he pleaded age.
proposals.after: Emperor Kang summoned him as Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance; again he pleaded age.
proposals.reason: The office 散騎常侍 is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Yu Liang recommended him with Zhai Tang; he ignored the doctorate call.
proposals.after: Yu Liang recommended him with Zhai Tang; he ignored the summons as Erudite.
proposals.reason: 博士 is the office Erudite rather than a doctorate.

proposals.before: The man would not keep it; Fan said, 'If you refuse, neither of us owns it.'
proposals.after: The man would not keep it; Fan said, 'If you had not retrieved it, how could I have gotten it?'
proposals.reason: The source argues that Fan recovered the knife only because the passerby retrieved it; it does not say neither man owns it.

proposals.before: Fan paid him tenfold the knife's worth and let him keep it.
proposals.after: Fan respected his wishes and paid him tenfold the knife's worth.
proposals.reason: 乃以十倍刀價與之 says Fan paid the man ten times the knife's value; it does not say he let the man keep the knife.

proposals.before: When Ran Min seized the throne and offered the grand astrologer post, Xin wrote to Min, saying, "In old days Xu You declined Yao and with the realm yielded to him, preserving his lofty and clean integrity.
proposals.after: When Ran Min seized the throne and offered the Grand Master of Ceremonies post, Xin wrote to Min, saying, "In old days Xu You declined Yao and with the realm yielded to him, preserving his lofty and clean integrity.
proposals.reason: 太常 is Grand Master of Ceremonies, not grand astrologer.

proposals.before: Chong heard and was greatly ashamed; thereupon he went to create his father.
proposals.after: Chong heard and was greatly ashamed; thereupon he went to visit his father.
proposals.reason: 造其父 means to go to or visit the father; 'create' is a lexical mistranslation.

proposals.before: Liu Yao named him grand astrologer; he fled to Longshan.
proposals.after: Liu Yao named him Grand Master of Ceremonies; he withdrew to Longshan.
proposals.reason: 太常 is Grand Master of Ceremonies, and the passage says he firmly declined and then lived in seclusion, not that he fled.

proposals.before: He answered no commandery summons; only with Yin Yong and Qi Liang was he friendly.
proposals.after: He answered no provincial or commandery summons; only with Yin Yong and Qi Hao was he friendly.
proposals.reason: 州郡 includes province and commandery, and 齊好 is Qi Hao; this complements the already-proposed idiomatic name repair.

proposals.before: His sixth-generation ancestor Zheng, in the Shun'an era of Han, the ducal offices summoned him eight times, the state carriage five times—he took none.
proposals.after: His sixth-generation ancestor Zheng, in the reigns of Emperors An and Shun of Han, was summoned eight times by the highest offices and five times by state carriage, but accepted none.
proposals.reason: 漢安順之世 refers to the reigns of Han Emperors An and Shun, not a 'Shun'an era.'

proposals.before: When rites were finished, he hid at Xie Valley of Linsong, chiseled a stone grotto and dwelt, ate cypress fruit to lighten the body, composed "Spring and Autumn Ink Discourse" and "Analects Mismatched Wefts"; disciples recorded numbered over a thousand.
